sentences.text: The skull of this creature measured approximately 21 centimeters in length.
Bruce Erickson named the species Albertochampsa langstoni in 1972.
Remains of this animal were a rare find within the fossil record.
This extinct animal is classified as an alligatorid, possibly representing a stem-caiman or a basal alligatorine.
A 2018 study placed Albertochampsa as more closely related to caimans within the subfamily Caimaninae.
However, a 2022 analysis by Walter et al. recovered it as one of the most basal alligatorines.
Albertochampsa lived in Alberta between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago during the Campanian stage.
Its fossils come from the Campanian-age Dinosaur Park Formation.
Scientists debate whether Albertochampsa is more closely related to modern alligators or caimans.
